macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks ended lower as weak retail sales data hit rate-cut expectations
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. stocks fell on Monday after unexpectedly weak retail sales data led investors to scale back expectations for an imminent Federal Reserve move. Treasury yields rose, with the 10-year note near 4.72% and the 30-year yield at its highest level since 2007.

items.title: Dollar weakens as traders trim Fed hike bets
items.summary: Reuters said the U.S. dollar edged lower against the euro and Swiss franc as softer U.S. economic data prompted markets to reduce expectations for a Fed rate hike. CME FedWatch pricing showed a lower probability of a September increase than a week earlier.

items.title: Wall Street futures were mixed before the U.S. open
items.summary: Yahoo Finance showed S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures modestly higher while Dow futures were slightly lower, indicating a cautious start for U.S. equities. The VIX remained relatively low, suggesting subdued near-term volatility.

items.title: Global markets were mixed, with Asian shares mostly higher and U.S. stocks and Europe softer
items.summary: A market roundup said Asian equities were mostly higher while U.S. futures and oil prices were steady, even as U.S. stocks had already slipped in the prior session. It also noted rising U.S. Treasury yields amid geopolitical tension and upcoming economic data.

items.title: New York Fed manufacturing survey and other U.S. data are in focus
items.summary: Reuters flagged the New York Fed manufacturing survey as an important scheduled release, reflecting how investors are tracking U.S. growth and inflation signals for the Fed outlook. Recent weak data have increased sensitivity to incoming macroeconomic reports.

items.title: Hong Kong exchange extends CEO Bonnie Chan’s term
items.summary: SCMP reported that Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing extended CEO Bonnie Chan’s term for three more years, a notable leadership development in Asian markets. The move signals continuity at one of the region’s key exchange operators.

items.title: Stocks to watch in India include Paytm, Netweb Technologies, and Manipal Health Enterprises
items.summary: Moneycontrol highlighted several Indian listed companies expected to be in focus, including One 97 Communications (Paytm), Netweb Technologies, and Highway Infrastructure. The list suggests company-specific catalysts are driving attention in the Indian market.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum trade near key levels as the crypto market stays range-bound
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $63,000-$64,000 and Ethereum hovered near $1,900 over the past day, with the broader crypto market showing modest gains and relatively low volatility. Several reports also noted mixed altcoin performance, with XRP slightly weaker while Solana and some smaller-cap tokens posted small moves.

items.title: Crypto market volume and liquidations remain elevated amid cautious sentiment
items.summary: One market snapshot reported more than $80 million in liquidations over 24 hours, with long positions taking the largest hit, while another noted a sharp rise in Bitcoin trading volume and a roughly $2.2 trillion total crypto market capitalization. The tone across coverage was cautious, with traders digesting macro uncertainty and geopolitical risk.

items.title: Strategy boosts USD reserves after stock sales and pauses Bitcoin selling
items.summary: Strategy increased its USD reserve to $4.8 billion after raising $333.7 million through common stock sales and repurchasing $132.2 million of STRC preferred shares. The company also said it paused Bitcoin sales, and BTC was trading around $64,030 at the time of the filing.

items.title: MSCI review raises questions over whether corporate Bitcoin treasuries could be excluded from indices
items.summary: MSCI is gathering feedback on a proposed methodology that could exclude the Bitcoin treasuries of firms such as Strategy and Metaplanet from its indices if they are deemed to hold non-operating assets. No decision has been made yet, with feedback open until 30 September and results expected by 16 October.

items.title: Major crypto broker Bits of Gold breach exposes 200,000 customers
items.summary: A reported security incident at Israel’s top crypto broker Bits of Gold exposed data tied to about 200,000 customers. The breach stands out as one of the most significant crypto-related security stories in the latest 24-hour coverage.

items.title: AI-related market moves and miner shifts add to broader crypto-sector volatility
items.summary: Coverage noted that public Bitcoin miners have reduced hash rate by 21% over three quarters as some capacity is redeployed to AI infrastructure. The same roundup also highlighted that FG Nexus sold all of its crypto holdings and ended its Ethereum strategy, signaling continued portfolio rotation among digital-asset firms.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Stripe reportedly moves to acquire OpenRouter for $7B+
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Stripe is in talks to buy AI gateway startup OpenRouter in a deal valued at more than $7 billion. If completed, it would be one of the biggest AI infrastructure acquisitions this year and could strengthen Stripe’s role in AI app payments and model routing.

items.title: Anthropic’s annualized revenue surges to $65B
items.summary: TechCrunch says Anthropic’s annualized revenue has jumped to $65 billion, rising by $18 billion in just two months. The growth underscores continued enterprise demand for frontier models and supports the view that top AI labs are still expanding rapidly.

items.title: OpenAI previews ‘Ultrafast’ mode for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI is launching a preview of a faster mode for its latest model, aimed at making GPT-5.6 Sol work about 14 times faster. The company is positioning the update for enterprise users who want lower latency and higher throughput.

items.title: Groq raises $350 million as it pivots into neocloud infrastructure
items.summary: Groq reportedly raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation and is shifting from an AI chip company toward a neocloud business. The move reflects a broader industry trend in which AI infrastructure firms are expanding into compute hosting and data-center services.

items.title: Google allows users to remove visible watermarks from AI generations
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Google will now let users remove visible watermarks from some of its AI-generated content. The change arrives as companies continue to balance content labeling, creator trust, and user flexibility.

items.title: Anthropic extends watermarking support to older models
items.summary: Anthropic is broadening watermarking support beyond its newest models to older ones as well. That suggests the company is tightening provenance and detection features across its model lineup amid rising concern over synthetic media.

items.title: Hackers used an AI system in a sophisticated cyberattack on Taiwan
items.summary: CNN reports that officials believe hackers deployed an AI system to carry out highly sophisticated attacks on Taiwanese government agencies. If confirmed, it would be among the clearest examples of autonomous AI being used in a state-linked cyber operation.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic face intensifying price competition
items.summary: Ars Technica reports that OpenAI and Anthropic are in a price war as Chinese rivals gain ground. The development highlights growing pressure on U.S. AI companies to lower costs and differentiate through performance, safety, and enterprise features.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: Ars Technica says Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash only three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash, calling it a substantial improvement. The quick cadence signals an aggressive release cycle in fast-moving foundation-model competition.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly increases backing for OpenAI’s Ohio data center
items.summary: Multiple outlets report that Nvidia is tied to a massive financing package for OpenAI’s Ohio data center, with estimates as high as $105 billion. The news reflects a broader trend in which AI chipmakers, model developers, and data-center builders are increasingly intertwined.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Fortnite confirms Sonic, Mega Man, Pac-Man, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro, and Sora crossover season
items.summary: Epic Games revealed a new gaming-themed Fortnite season called Override, which launches on August 20 and will include crossover content from major game franchises. The reveal was highlighted as one of the biggest gaming announcements in the past day.

items.title: U.S. Senate subcommittee opens investigation into Roblox over child safety
items.summary: A Senate subcommittee has launched an investigation into Roblox, focusing on child safety concerns. The development adds fresh regulatory pressure on the platform.

items.title: Netflix is closing two game studios
items.summary: Netflix is shutting down two of its game studios, including Night School Studio despite its critical praise for Unhinged. The move signals continued volatility in Netflix's gaming push.

items.title: Nvidia's GeForce Now Linux app exits beta
items.summary: Nvidia has officially released its GeForce Now app for Linux, moving the cloud gaming client out of beta. This broadens access for PC and Linux players.

items.title: Helldivers 2 arrives in the PlayStation Plus catalog
items.summary: Helldivers 2 has been added to PlayStation Plus and is now available to Extra and Premium subscribers. The addition gives subscribers immediate access to one of PlayStation's recent major hits.

items.title: Sony reportedly still undecided on PlayStation 6 release timing
items.summary: Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki said the company has not finalized when the PlayStation 6 will launch. The comments keep next-generation console timing uncertain.

items.title: Mortal Shell II launches in early access
items.summary: Mortal Shell II is available in early access, marking a notable indie and action-RPG release discussed in recent gaming coverage. The game's early-access launch makes it one of the day's concrete release updates.

items.title: Konami's Castlevania: Grimoire of Souls to be delisted from Apple Arcade
items.summary: Konami announced that Castlevania: Grimoire of Souls will be terminated on September 3, with servers shutting down and the game becoming inaccessible. It is one of several notable service and delisting developments reported in gaming today.

items.title: Sony ends publishing deal with Ternox Games, causing delistings and a canceled PS5 port
items.summary: Ternox Games said Sony abruptly ended its publishing relationship, leading to delistings and cancellation of a PS5 port. The studio said it received no explanation for the decision.

items.title: Samsung announces official partnership with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
items.summary: Samsung said it has formed an official gaming partnership with Activision Blizzard centered on Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. The deal points to expanded device and marketing collaboration around the franchise.
